newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler economist says dollar/yen hurting.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler economist says dollar/yen hurting.

text.p: Chrysler Corp chief economist Van Bussmann said Friday the surge in the dollar against the yen is starting to hurt U.S. automaker competitiveness.

"It's starting to hurt," Bussmann said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "We see a real upsurge in the share of Japanese cars as a percentage of what's sold here and of course if that goes on, then we'll have to cut production, because they will have an unnecessary advantage over us, and we're likely to lose some jobs over that."
Japanese firms could gain several percentage points in the U.S. car market as a result of the dollar's strength, Bussmann said.
"They lost about four or five percentage points over the prior four years and they could easily gain back that whole share, depending on how long this ultra-weak yen lasts," he said.
"We think that the dollar should be left to determine its value by markets and not through government intervention," Bussmann said.
